summary: Both paths are started and neither has drawn a character. This records exactly what holds and what does not.

A_confirms.device and swapchain: verified: vtable matches Direct3D11.dll+0x175E8, CreatePrimarySurface returns a surface, BeginFrame returns 1, Clear plus PresentSurface shows a pure colour that reproduces
A_confirms.archive layer: verified: Attach returns 1, GetNumFiles is 3341, OpenFile on Creatures/pc/hero_00.msh returns a File whose index reads 2461
A_confirms.byte range: verified twice, statically and at runtime: offset 399226753, stored 111402, raw 223717
A_confirms.payload: extracted 111350 bytes of plain binary, 66.7 percent plausible floats, tail holds pi/2, pi and pi/6

A_blocked_on.read_trigger: I called the ArchiveFile vtable slot 2 with (0, 223717); it returned without fault but [[file+8]+0x10] still did not contain geometry, so slot 2 is probably a position or bounds routine rather than the read that materialises the payload
A_blocked_on.vertex_format: still unknown, and this is the real blocker for A

B_started.found: Character::Character() at 0x52030 is exported; Actor constructors are not
B_started.prerequisite: a Character needs the world, the object manager and a graphics scene to exist first, so B begins by driving those rather than by loading a model

why_i_stopped_trying_variants: Each further blind attempt at a vtable slot or a buffer offset has a low chance of being the right one and a real chance of producing a plausible looking but wrong result. The next productive step is reading the mesh loader statically, not more probing.
recommended: decode the internal mesh loader: search Game.dll for the routine that consumes a block whose magic is MSH, which yields the vertex declaration directly. That single piece unblocks both A and B.
